Contentexpand_moreexpand_lessLearning objectives and content
    ObjectivesUnderstands the concepts and axiomatics of a vector space and its dual in the finite-dimensional setting in relation to the Kronecker tensor formalism and the distinction between covariant, contravariant and mixed tensors. 

Can use tensor calculus to represent general tensors relative to an appropriate basis. Tensors of particular interest are: Kronecker tensor, (Riemannian and Lorentzian) metric tensor, torsion tensor, curvature tensor, Levi-Civita tensor.

Understands common notational issues such as holor symbols, ad hoc polymorphism and summation convention and can routinely manipulate these.

Understands the concept of a differentiable manifold and that of a general vector bundle and sections of it, notably tensor fields.

Understands how abstract geometric definitions are related to basis and coordinate chart induced numerical (holonomic or anholonomic) representations. 

Understands various geometrically meaningful point and derivative operators acting on tensor fields, notably musical isomorphism, Hodge star, Lie derivative, exterior derivative, covariant derivative (in relation to a linear connection) and the standard, symmetric and antisymmetric tensor product. 

Develops strong heuristics concerning the meaning of all abstract geometric concepts by applying these to solve practical and fundamental problems in various physical science and engineering domains when given a short introductory explanation of the context. A non-exhaustive list includes cartography, cosmology (cosmic expansion, red shift, cosmic background radiation), special and general relativity theory (planets and stars, black holes, neutron stars, gravitational waves, dark energy, geodesics), continuum mechanics and deformation analysis, particle physics, field theories, image analysis, image restoration, psychophysics, visual perception, computational neuroscience and neuroanatomy, classical physics. 
    ContentBasic linear algebra, recap, with a focus on vector space axioms and the definition of a matrix  determinant. 

Manifolds: Charts and atlases, transition maps, active versus passive transformations.

Vector bundles: Tangent and cotangent bundle and general vector bundles, sections (tensor fields) and holor representations. Focus on important instances, notably Kronecker tensor, torsion, curvature, metric and volume form, and on typical constraints, notably symmetry/antisymmetry. Hodge star duality.

Differential operators: Linear connections with application to parallel transport, exterior derivative, Lie derivative. The role of partial derivatives and differentials.

Riemannian and Lorentzian manifolds: Metrics, geodesics, Levi-Civita connection, holor index raising and lowering induced by the musical isomorphism.
